issues.legal_issue: Enhanced compensation does not accrue as taxable income while the right to receive it remains genuinely disputed in an appeal.
material_facts: The landowner received an arbitrator’s award enhancing compensation for land acquired by the government.
The government appealed the award, challenging the enhanced compensation while the appeal remained pending.
The government deposited the disputed amount, but the landowner could withdraw it only after furnishing security for repayment if the appeal succeeded.
The amount was credited to a suspense account, and the tax authority sought to include it in business income for the relevant assessment year.
issues.conclusion: The disputed enhanced compensation had not accrued as income during the relevant previous year and was not taxable in that assessment year; the Revenue’s appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4(1)(b)(i) of the Income-tax Act, 1922 (and the corresponding accrual concept in section 5(1)(b) of the Income-tax Act, 1961), income accrues when a right to receive it creates a debt due; a mere claim to additional compensation does not suffice while entitlement itself remains in dispute. This differs from a case where the right to payment is admitted and only quantification remains. The Court applied E.D. Sassoon & Company Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay City, and relied on Commissioner of Income-tax v. Jai Parkash Om Parkash Co. Ltd., Khan Bahadur Ahmed Alladin & Sons v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Topandas Kundanmal v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Additional Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat v. New Jehangir Vakil Mills Co. Ltd., and Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer. Kedarnath Jute Mfg. Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Pope The King Match Factory v. Commissioner of Income-tax were distinguished because those cases concerned liabilities whose existence was not in dispute and whose quantification alone remained to be determined.

rule.if: tax_accrual_case and enhanced_compensation_claim and government_appealed_entitlement and (appeal_challenged_entitlement or withdrawal_required_security)

predicates.tax_accrual_case: The proceeding concerns whether income accrued for a tax assessment period.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_claim: A landowner claims additional compensation for land acquired by the government.
predicates.government_appealed_entitlement: The government appealed an award granting the additional compensation and challenged the landowner’s entitlement to it.
predicates.appeal_challenged_entitlement: The pending appeal put the right to receive the additional compensation, rather than merely its amount, in dispute.
predicates.withdrawal_required_security: The landowner was permitted to withdraw the deposited disputed amount only after providing security for its repayment.

issues.definition: When a tax accrual proceeding concerns a claim for enhanced land compensation and the government’s appeal disputes entitlement or withdrawal depends on security, the enhanced compensation is treated as not accrued.
